findings.title: Default `queued` evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource shares the same stale timestamp. It should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Also, `asdict` leaves a datetime in the dict. The dict is passed as Celery task kwargs, which may fail JSON serialization or come back as a string.

findings.title: from_dict round trip is unsafe with serialized `queued`
findings.body: `to_dict` produces a datetime for `queued`. After the task serializer round trip it may arrive as a string or be unserializable. `from_dict` passes it straight into the constructor with no parsing. Unexpected extra keys raise TypeError, which is swallowed and returns None. That silently disables the cycle-breaking.

findings.title: Abstract signatures changed and callers not updated
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`. The abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` only accepts `**kwargs`, so it is fine there. But the `sync_status_outbound` signature was changed without any caller or implementation being updated, which is unrelated to the fix. Implementations that don't accept the new keyword in a compatible way may break.

findings.title: No test that inbound sync passes the assignment source
findings.body: The tests only call assign with a manually built source. Nothing verifies that `sync_group_assignee_inbound` now passes `AssignmentSource.from_integration`, which is the actual cycle fix. Nothing covers the deassign path with a matching source either.
